subject: Replacement cost justification & swap timeline for BrightLane
messages:

Date: 2026-11-18T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Replacement economics & timeline

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and I have pulled together a quick ask: we need a clear cost-justification vs our incumbent (ApexCompute) and a realistic 90-day swap timeline. Apex has offered a 25% first-year discount + a 6-week migration support credit.

Specifically can you:
- Lay out a 12- / 24- / 36-month pricing comparison (list unit rates and effective unit cost after discounts).
- Show migration credits or onboarding offsets you can commit to (one-time credits, credit schedule, egress assistance).
- Confirm what packaging (dedicated vs hosted) makes sense for our peak inference workloads (50 rps, 8B model family).

We also need any procurement-friendly collateral (SOW, term sheet) for our legal team.

Appreciate a candid view — we want parity or better on economics to present to leadership.

Best,
Oliver
Head of ML Ops
BrightLane Health
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@brightlanehealth.com>
Cc: Samira Qureshi <samira@brightlanehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Replacement economics & timeline

Thanks Oliver — great to connect. High-level response below and I attached a one-page SOW + a swap economics worksheet with the line-item math.

Quick take (will expand if you want a formal POC pricing doc):
- Packaging recommendation: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) with a burst to Hosted for peak days. This gives predictable latency and >10% unit-cost savings vs hosted at your projected 50 rps.
- Pricing comparison, net effective first-year:
  - 12-month: 18% discount on list; onboarding credit = $40k; estimated net savings vs Apex = ~8% (Apex uses a seat-based + egress model).
  - 24-month: 22% discount + $60k credit; net savings vs Apex = ~15% and we commit to a 99.9% uptime SLA for the Dedicated pool.
  - 36-month: 28% discount + $100k migration/egress credit; net savings vs Apex = ~24% plus inclusion of 200k pre-committed inference tokens (to offset ramp).
- Migration support: 6-week technical runway, plus an optional 8-week dedicated onboarding bundle (engineer hours + integration tests). We can structure credits to pay down the first two invoices if that helps procurement cashflow.
- Escape hatch / rollback: we propose a phased cutover by customer region with a canary window and explicit rollback milestones (we include rollback criteria in the SOW).

Attachments: BrightLane_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW + rollback milestones), swap_econ_worksheet.xlsx (line-by-line), redwood-dedicated-term-sheet.docx (term highlights).

If this looks directionally right I can run numbers with Finance for a binding quote and a limited-time switch credit. Happy to hop on a call to walk through the worksheet.

Warmly,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Replacement economics & timeline — BrightLane request + worksheet

Karthik / Tessa — forwarding BrightLane's ask and the worksheet I shared. Key asks from procurement: match/beat Apex's 25% first-year discount and deliver a 90-day swap path.

My proposal:
- Offer A (Aggressive): 30% first-year effective discount (applies to Dedicated list), $100k migration/egress credit, 36-month term, 200k pre-committed tokens. Requires approval for revenue write-down and a 10% margin buffer.
- Offer B (Balanced): 22% first-year discount, $60k credit, 24-month term, 100k pre-committed tokens, standard SLA.
- Offer C (Conservative): 18% first-year discount, $40k credit, 12-month term, limited onboarding add-on (billed), no token precommit.

Other levers: quick-pay discount (additional 3% if prepay 6 months), engineering day cap (we can include 5 days free for integration, additional days billable), and a one-time onboarding credit applied against first invoice.

Decision points I need from you:
1) Approve Offer A for Sales Exec signoff (requires finance to agree to margin impact).
2) If Offer A not approved, confirm counter threshold for Offer B.
3) Any redlines on rollback/indemnity we should avoid in the SOW.

I think BrightLane is a strong strategic logo (healthcare + sensitive data) — Private deployment appetite later might be an upsell.

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren — quick notes from finance and ops after reviewing the worksheet:

- Offer A (30% + $100k) is borderline but doable if we get a 36-month committed ARR and a clear engineering resource plan. Finance wants a minimum 8% blended margin protection; we can use quantization guidance and runtime packing to protect cost.
- Suggest including a staged billing credit: $60k applied first month, $40k applied month 7, to preserve cash visibility.
- Ops notes: 90-day swap is aggressive but possible with a staffed migration plan. We should commit to a canary in week 4 and full cutover by week 9 to give ops buffer.
- Legal flag: procurement asked for a clause limiting service credits to 5x daily token cost — legal prefers capping to limit exposure. Keep this as negotiable.

Recommendation: approve Offer B as the public-facing starting point, with Offer A as an executive-level counter if BrightLane pushes. If Sales wants to lead with Offer A, we need a one-page CFO sign-off template to expedite approval.
